fases.texto_objetivo: First step on the lunar surface
Installation of the lunar scientific experiment

ficha_info.texto: American pilot and astronaut (1930-2012). He commanded the ==Apollo 11== mission and, on July 20, 1969, was the first human to set foot on the Moon.

frases: ==That's one small step for man, but one giant leap for mankind==.
The goal was to place the lunar module and collect scientific data from the surface.

opciones.etiqueta: What kind of data was collected?
opciones.respuesta: The composition of the regolith and the temperature were measured.

opciones.etiqueta: Why was the lunar mission important?
opciones.respuesta: It proved that humanity could reach another celestial body.

frases: In zero gravity, every step requires precise control of momentum.
We deployed the ==American flag== as a symbol of the national achievement.
The module's solar panels provide energy to the instruments during the lunar night.

opciones.etiqueta: How does solar power work on the Moon?
opciones.respuesta: The panels convert sunlight into electricity, storing it in batteries.

opciones.etiqueta: What happens when the Moon is in darkness?
opciones.respuesta: The systems use the stored energy to keep the equipment operational.

frases: This act stirred pride throughout the nation and showed the power of collaborative science.
We installed the ==EASEP== experiment, which includes a ==passive seismometer== and ==laser retroreflectors== to measure the Earth-Moon distance.
The retroreflectors let ground stations send lasers and calculate the distance with millimeter precision.

opciones.etiqueta: Why is it important to measure the Earth-Moon distance?
opciones.respuesta: It helps calibrate the orbit and test the theory of relativity.

opciones.etiqueta: How are seismometers used on the Moon?
opciones.respuesta: They record internal tremors that reveal the satellite's internal structure.

frases: The data collected will expand our knowledge of lunar seismic activity.

acciones.descripcion: Neil describes the function of the ==Eagle Module== as a lunar descent and ascent vehicle.

ficha_info.texto: Pilot of the Eagle lunar module and second man to walk on the Moon. He contributed to the engineering of the life-support systems and to the installation of scientific experiments.

frases: I planted the second ==American flag== while Neil secured it.
The Eagle module is equipped with life-support systems that work in the vacuum and maintain internal pressure.

opciones.etiqueta: How is the pressure inside the suit controlled?
opciones.respuesta: The suits use air-recycling systems and regulated pressure to sustain life.

opciones.etiqueta: What challenges arose from operating in the vacuum?
opciones.respuesta: The lunar dust and the lack of atmosphere make handling the equipment difficult.

frases: Seeing the Earth from the Moon reminded me of the fragility of our planet.
I helped install the ==passive seismometer== and the ==laser retroreflectors== of the ==EASEP== project.
The retroreflectors return the laser beam to Earth, creating a permanent reference point.

opciones.respuesta: Five reflectors were installed across the lunar surface.

opciones.etiqueta: How long did the laser calibration take?
opciones.respuesta: The calibration took several days of fine adjustments from the observatories.

frases: Each measurement brings us closer to better understanding the geology of the Moon.

acciones.descripcion: Buzz activates the ==Passive Seismometer== to record lunar vibrations.

interaccion.descripcion: Image-capture device that broadcasts in real time to Earth. It uses a CCD sensor and an antenna to send video data via radio waves.
Flag of synthetic fabric in red, white and blue. It is designed to stay extended in the vacuum by means of a telescopic pole and a horizontal bar that holds it.

Apollo Surface Experiments Package, a set of instruments to measure seismic activity, laser reflection and other variables. Each component is mounted on a leveled base to ensure stability in low gravity.
Motion sensor that records vibrations of the lunar surface by means of a suspended mass. The data is stored in an internal memory for later transmission.
Set of prisms that return the laser beam emitted from Earth. They allow the Earth-Moon distance to be measured with centimeter precision through the photon's time of flight.

interaccion.texto_activacion: The solar panels deploy and begin to emit a soft blue glow.
interaccion.texto_desactivacion: The panels shut down, leaving only the lunar surface in silence.

interaccion.descripcion: A basalt fragment from the Mare Tranquillitatis in its sealed container. One of the samples the Apollo 11 crew brought back to Earth for study.

zonas_narrativas.texto: As I cross the threshold of the ==Eagle Module==, the lunar dust rises and the gray surface stretches out beneath the black sky.
